- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >70% of recent days negative), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound potential.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid over-optimism.
- In high-sentiment volatility periods (e.g., sentiment swings >0.5), model underreacts to short-term momentum — increase forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment shifts, especially if sentiment turns positive.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early forecast windows — if 30d forecast is significantly below recent 18d average, adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect momentum.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often underestimates continuation — increase forecast by 3–5% for 3–5 day horizon if sentiment >0.7 and price >35.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates depth — add 2–5% buffer below true low to avoid premature bottoming.
- In multi-day event windows (e.g., policy changes, emissions targets), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of event if sentiment indicates urgency or policy impact.
